consolidation_2026_09_03.materialization: fd6e20f replaced the v5.1 bootstrap. The bootstrap was FOUR commits -- 26c563b, b6a42a6, 6c94adb and b7b2cbe -- carrying ten binary parts under .v51-bootstrap/ plus .github/workflows/tgsa-v5-1-bootstrap.yml, a contents:write workflow that reassembled a tarball, verified it, and force-pushed a materialized commit. It failed FOUR times (runs 33699105352, 33699971132, 33700347537, 33772927517), and no failure was scientific. Run 33700347537, the THIRD, is the well-known one: all 444 tests, contract verification, schema validation and the probe+qualification smoke chain passed and it printed 'bootstrap validation passed for the exact final v5.1 tree', then it died on `git diff --check` because V5_1_UNIFIED_PROGRAMME.md lines 3 and 4 end in two trailing spaces (Markdown hard breaks). That permission boundary, not the whitespace guard, is what finally ended the bootstrap route.

The first confirmed 2 errors, the second 13 (five root causes), the third -- run uncapped -- confirmed 16 of 28 candidates, reducing to the seven corrected here plus four in the Stage 0 plan document. The single high-severity finding was not in the ledger at all: the Stage 0 plan's qualification commands omitted the mandatory --frozen-band argument and the select_phase1_v5_1.py capacity step that produces it, so every qualification invocation would have raised V5ContractError before creating output. Development-only smoke runs could not have caught it, because _validate_frozen_band returns early when development_only is true. verify_programme_ledger.py catches none of this class of error: it checks imported-file hashes and stage-commit resolution, never counts, run histories, cross-branch byte-identity, or command validity.

consolidation_2026_09_04.apparatus_review: three adversarial review passes were run against the v5 apparatus and the fixes to it. The first swept scoring, nulls, arm isolation, gates, determinism and data generation: 19 candidates, 4 confirmed, 3 of them high. consolidation_2026_09_04.review_accounting_bug: the first review reported 'confirmed: []' with every candidate counted as refuted, which read as a clean apparatus. It was not: four refuters had died and returned null verdicts, and the tally counted null as refuted. Two finder dimensions had not run at all. Re-run with unadjudicated tracked separately, the same review returned 4 confirmed defects including 3 high. A verification harness that cannot distinguish 'refuted' from 'never checked' will report a clean result for work it never examined.
consolidation_2026_09_04.lesson: two of the four defects were invisible to every test the programme permits at this stage, because development mode bypasses the code that was wrong: _validate_frozen_band returns early when development_only is true, so no smoke run could reach the missing --frozen-band, and the smoke plan's null is low enough that the below-chance seed hole never opened. stage0_preflight_audit.why: Stage 0 is a prospective registration and running it before the lock destroys that registration irrecoverably, so the last cheap moment to find an apparatus or runbook defect is BEFORE the operator attests. The 2026-09-04 round had already found one defect of the only class that matters here -- a command defect invisible to every permitted test, because the code it would have tripped is behind `if not development_only`. This audit went looking for more of that class.
stage0_preflight_audit.method: static, read-only, no pipeline execution and no attestation flag. Seven dimensions fanned out over the dev-unreachable surface (ten sites), verbatim command-vs-argparse validity, plan/contract/schema required-array integrity, the five-step probe->band->qualification data flow, threshold arithmetic direction, resume/idempotency contamination, and attestation plumbing. Each finding faced three adversarial refuters on distinct lenses.

confirmed_finding.title: STAGE0_EXECUTION_PLAN.md section 4.0 told the operator to point --report at the passing rung only; the ladder is not skippable, so the band cannot be frozen whenever C1 is not the rung that passes
confirmed_finding.severity: high, but fail-closed: nothing is destroyed and recovery is a re-run
confirmed_finding.mechanism: freeze_band_after_probe (tgsa/phase1_v5.py:1077-1087) walks the registered ladder C1 -> C2 -> C3 from the FIRST rung and raises 'probe report for rung <X> is missing; rung selection must follow the registered order' the moment a rung has no report. A failing rung's report is still required -- it is the evidence the climb was registered. A NO_GO rung yields decision ADVANCE_CAPACITY_RUNG, which is deliberately NOT among the loop's break conditions (REJECT_SATURATED_BAND, REJECT_TASK_FAMILY), so the loop advances and demands the next rung's report too. Symmetrically a report AFTER the first pass is refused. The doc stated neither constraint.
confirmed_finding.why_no_test_caught_it: for the registered plan freeze_band_after_probe raises 'development-only probe reports cannot freeze a real band' at tgsa/phase1_v5.py:1075, BEFORE the ladder loop is entered, so no development-mode run can reach the missing-report check. And every freeze_band_after_probe test in tests/test_phase1_v5.py uses C1 as the passing rung, so the 'C1 failed, a later rung passed' path has no coverage at all.
confirmed_finding.failure_scenario: probe C1 returns NO_GO/ADVANCE_CAPACITY_RUNG after ~0.79 h; probe C2 returns GO after ~1.60 h; the operator runs section 4.0 verbatim per the old note, supplying only probe_C2's report; the selector raises V5ContractError naming rung C1, writes no frozen_band.json, and the entire 36-cell / 1.08 M-step qualification is blocked with the doc pointing away from the fix.
confirmed_finding.verified_how: confirmed by direct reading of the code, the argparse definitions, the registered plan's ladder (rung ids C1/C2/C3, development_only false) and the test suite -- not accepted on a subagent's report. Two of three adversarial refuters also confirmed it; the third died on the session limit.
confirmed_finding.fix: documentation only; the code is correct and needs no change. --report is action='append' on both the capacity and exposure subcommands (scripts/select_phase1_v5_1.py:79,85), so repetition was always supported. Section 4.0 now states the rule (one --report per rung from C1 up to and including the pass, in order, none after it), shows the two-report form, and records why no test covers it.
confirmed_finding.residual_recommendation: the C1-fails-then-C2-passes ladder path still has zero test coverage. Adding that test would touch C11, the frozen registration tree, so it is left as an operator decision rather than done unilaterally. It is not required to make Stage 0 safe -- the code already enforces the rule correctly; only the runbook was wrong.

stage0_preflight_audit.accounting_bug_RECURRED: the review_accounting_bug recorded under 2026-09-04 happened again, in the audit harness itself. The workflow's survivor rule was `confirmed >= 2 || (confirmed >= 1 && refuted == 0)`, so a finding whose three refuters ALL died scored confirmed=0 and fell into the 'refuted' bucket despite never having been examined. Seven findings were mislabelled that way. The run was only readable because the harness ALSO tracked unadjudicated separately and emitted an incomplete_adjudication list, which is the only reason the mislabelling was visible rather than silent. Lesson, restated because restating it did not prevent it: a three-way verdict (confirmed / refuted / never-checked) must be carried all the way into the FINAL bucketing, not just into the tally. Defaulting an unexamined finding to 'refuted' turns a dead verifier into a clean bill of health.
